title: Tamsin and the Oath
premise: Zephyrine Iversen, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has survived seven years in the city of Vaelhollow by selling harmless charms and hiding her gift from the Wardens who outlawed magic. When a blind date named Corin turns out to be pictured in a century-old book of prophecies—beside her own face—she is dragged into a plot to unbind King Aldric from the ancient thing that has worn his crown for thirty years. As Zephyrine gathers allies among the dead and the dispossessed, she learns the crown-thing feeds on belonging, twisting love into leash and loyalty into chains. In the end she must choose between destroying the crown and becoming its new vessel; she shatters it at the cost of her hearing, going deaf to the dead but finally free to belong among the living.
about_author: Silas Crane is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring medieval reliquaries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about objects that remember, and live quietly with too many carved bones and one judgmental cat.

chapters.title: The Charmseller's Hour
chapters.summary: Zephyrine carves a mourning charm for a widow while listening to the dead woman's husband complain about the wallpaper. Her POV establishes her double life: licensed bone-carver by day, illegal hearer of the dead by night. Emotional beat: weary tenderness, and the loneliness of being a secret in a city that fears what she is.

chapters.title: A Date with Prophecy
chapters.summary: Corin, charming and oddly formal over dinner, mentions a dream he's had since childhood. Zephyrine's POV: when he describes it, she recognizes the imagery from a forbidden prophecy book she once catalogued. Emotional beat: dread blooming under flirtation—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine breaks into the Warden archive with her dead mentor's guidance and finds the prophecy ledger: her own likeness sketched beside Corin's, dated a century past. His POV briefly intrudes—he followed her. Emotional beat: vertigo; her carefully built life revealed as someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Crown
chapters.summary: Through a relic of the old queen, Zephyrine hears the truth: King Aldric died years ago, and something ancient wears his shape, feeding on the city's devotion. Corin's POV as he confesses he was sent to find her. Emotional beat: horror tempered by an unlikely alliance forming.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: The Wardens raid Zephyrine's shop, tipped off by an informant. She escapes through the bone-cellars with Corin's help, leaving seven years of work burning behind her. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life, and the first spark of fury aimed upward.

chapters.title: The Undercity of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: They descend to Vaelhollow's forgotten levels, where unregistered magic-users survive. Zephyrine meets Maren, a fire-singer who tends the last captive dragon's dying flame. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: cautious wonder—belonging offered, not yet trusted.

chapters.title: Lessons in Listening
chapters.summary: Maren teaches Zephyrine that the dead aren't echoes but witnesses, and that the crown-thing silences them deliberately. Zephyrine's POV as she hears, for the first time, the chorus of everyone the crown has erased. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Corin's Hundred Years
chapters.summary: Corin reveals he is older than he looks—a man the prophecy pulled forward, kept young as bait. His POV: shame at being a lure, tenderness toward the woman he was sent to catch. Emotional beat: betrayal confessed, forgiveness withheld but possible.

chapters.title: The Dragon's Guttering
chapters.summary: The last dragon-fire, source of all true binding magic, is failing in its Warden vault. Zephyrine visits it and hears the dragon's final memories, including how Aldric once bound the crown-thing. Her POV. Emotional beat: urgency—the clock is now literal.

chapters.title: A Court of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Invited (summoned) to court, Zephyrine plays charm-seller before the king and feels the crown-thing notice her, tasting her gift like a tongue. Her POV, terror masked as deference. Emotional beat: the predator and prey recognize each other across a throne room.

chapters.title: The Informant's Face
chapters.summary: Zephyrine discovers the traitor who reported her: a dead friend's voice, still bound in service to the crown. His POV posthumously, via the relic she carries. Emotional beat: heartbreak—corruption shown as intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: Leashes Made of Love
chapters.summary: The crown-thing offers Zephyrine a bargain: her mentor restored, her hearing honored, in exchange for delivering Corin. Her POV wrestling with temptation. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—power corrupts by offering exactly what you most want.

chapters.title: Riot of the Quiet
chapters.summary: Maren and the undercity launch a diversion, freeing the dragon-vault while Wardens hunt Zephyrine. Multiple POVs converge in a night of fire and bells. Emotional beat: exhilaration and cost—the first open rebellion, and its first deaths.

chapters.title: What Maren Burned
chapters.summary: Maren's backstory: she once served the crown willingly and burned her own village's records to hide her family. Her POV. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into fierce protectiveness of Zephyrine and Corin.

chapters.title: The Dead Go Silent
chapters.summary: The crown-thing strikes back, severing Zephyrine's connection to the dead city-wide—an act of mass erasure. Her POV in sudden, terrible quiet. Emotional beat: isolation as violence; the lowest point begins.

chapters.title: Deaf to Everything But Him
chapters.summary: Cut off from her gift, Zephyrine must trust only the living—and chooses Corin, fully, despite his role as bait. His POV watching her choose him without magic's crutch. Emotional beat: love as decision, not enchantment.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: They decode the ledger's final page: the prophecy never named a hero—it named a vessel. The crown intends Zephyrine as its next wearer. Her POV. Emotional beat: cold clarity; destiny reframed as trap.

chapters.title: Storming the Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: The assault on the palace: Maren's fire, the undercity's numbers, Corin's knowledge of the wards he helped design. Multi-POV set-piece. Emotional beat: desperate courage rising toward the climax.

chapters.title: Audience with the Wearer
chapters.summary: Alone before the king-thing, Zephyrine hears Aldric's true ghost, buried beneath decades of stolen devotion, and learns the crown can be shattered only by one who refuses it. Her POV. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster's prisoner.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Climax: the crown-thing offers her everything—her dead, her mentor, a kingdom that belongs to her. Zephyrine refuses aloud, and with the guttering dragon-fire's last breath, shatters the crown. The blast takes her hearing entirely. Her POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Aldric's ghost, freed, thanks her and fades; Vaelhollow wakes to a kingless dawn and must govern itself. Zephyrine, deaf to the dead, grieves and heals among the living. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Oath
chapters.summary: Epilogue: taking the name Tamsin from the prophecy's last line, she reopens a carving shop—not charms now, but honest craft—and swears an oath with Corin and Maren to guard against any crown that whispers. Her POV. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely; identity authored, not assigned.
